kinds.d: Calcium iron aluminium silicate hydroxide specimen: pistachio-green striated prisms; epidote also forms the green of unakite.

x.d: Magnificent dark green long-prismatic crystals from the Knappenwand, Untersulzbachtal, Salzburg.
Large dark green tabular crystals with copper ores from Prince of Wales Island, Alaska.
Exceptional epidote crystals from Tormiq, Pakistan.
Ornamental rock of green epidote, pink feldspar and quartz.
Epidote from Bourg d'Oisans, Isère, France.

kinds.d: Calcium aluminium silicate hydroxide specimen: tanzanite blue crystals, pink thulite and anyolite; named for Sigmund Zois.

x.d: Blue to violet gem variety of zoisite from Tanzania.
Pink manganese-bearing zoisite from Norway, also found at the Jeffrey mine, Quebec.
Ruby-in-zoisite rock named variety from Kenya; the Tanzania source is described under Corundum.
Type-locality zoisite from the Saualpe, Carinthia, first called saualpite; described by Werner in 1805.
Exceptional gem zoisite from the Merelani Hills, Lelatema Mountains, Tanzania.

kinds.d: Calcium magnesium aluminium silicate specimen: tetragonal crystals in green, brown or blue; californite is a jade-like massive form.

x.d: Jade-like massive vesuvianite, also sold as California jade.
Sky-blue copper-coloured vesuvianite from Franklin, New Jersey.
Manganese-rich vesuvianite.
Green vesuvianite crystals from the Jeffrey mine, Val-des-Sources (Asbestos), Quebec.
Type-locality vesuvianite from Monte Somma; named by Werner in 1795.
Vesuvianite from the Ala Valley, Piedmont.

kinds.d: Hydrous zinc silicate specimen: white or blue sprays and botryoidal crusts; hemimorphic crystals and the old 'calamine'.

x.d: Blue botryoidal crusts, e.g. from Wenshan, Yunnan and Mapimí, Durango, shown on Wikipedia.
Historic name for mixed hemimorphite and smithsonite ore; the two were separated in the later 18th century.
Hemimorphite from Moresnet, Belgium, and Altenberg.
Hemimorphite from Franklin and Sterling Hill, New Jersey.
Large hemimorphite crystals from Nerchinsk, Siberia.
Hemimorphite from Elkhorn, Montana, and Leadville, Colorado.

kinds.d: Calcium iron silicate hydroxide specimen: black prismatic crystals and columnar masses, first described from Elba in 1811.

x.d: Type-locality ilvaite from Rio Marina and Capo Calamita, Elba, first described in 1811.
Very large ilvaite crystals from Seriphos, Cyclades.
Fine ilvaite crystals from Dal'negorsk, Primorsky Krai.
Splendid ilvaite crystals from the Laxey mine, Owyhee County, Idaho.
Ilvaite from the Kamioka mine, Gifu, Japan.

notes: All 5 planned kinds kept. Sources: Wikipedia and HOM. Merelani and the 1967 tanzanite discovery/Tiffany link are not on the fetched Zoisite page and are omitted. No brands or traditions.
